assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the universe and answers a century-old cosmic-ray question with clues from nature, not from elegant theory. It is a discovery-first case: a new kind of astronomy, with an existential dimension in probing the most violent accelerators.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and its 2013 observation, so a single-laureate configuration is defensible from the supplied credit. The list offers no other credited name, so the extent of credit owed to collaborators and the earlier detector pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND) cannot be judged from this entry.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux, the later TXS 0506+056 coincidence and the Galactic-plane neutrino map by IceCube strengthen the case; the flux is stable and the field is established. Timing looks reasonable, though source identification is still incomplete.
uncertainties: Whether a one-person prize fairly reflects a large collaboration and the detector pioneers.
Cosmic-ray source identification is still only partial, and I am relying on memory of the individual results rather than verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. It is original, clear and has had very large impact, with a direct confirm-by-experiment structure.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery, which gives a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Cao and others in the experimental team, and the earlier Lopes dos Santos and Peres work, are open attribution questions, and the supplied names do not include them.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon has been reproduced by many groups worldwide and the field is mature and stable. Recognition would be timely, as the field is still developing fast, although the pairing mechanism in the superconducting state is not yet settled.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for the earlier theory of twisted-bilayer band structure and for junior experimentalists is potentially disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the resulting concept of topological insulators changed how condensed-matter physics classifies phases. Importance, originality and lasting impact are high, and the field is the natural successor to the 2016 topological-phase prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal and Molenkamp's group made the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The trio is a good theory-experiment fit, but Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents, and others, make credit allocation contestable.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is robust and independent, including three-dimensional topological insulators, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably already somewhat late.
uncertainties: Several theorists with comparable claims are not in the supplied credited names for this candidate.
I am recalling the sequence of predictions and experiments from memory and have not verified exact priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision measurements of the CMB anisotropy that established the cosmological parameters of the Lambda-CDM model, and it gave strong, observational evidence for dark energy and a flat universe. This is a discovery-driven result that I would regard as foundational for modern cosmology, and I like having clues from nature behind the dark-energy picture.
assessment.attribution: Bennett as principal investigator, Page as an instrument and observational leader, and Spergel as the lead on the data analysis and cosmological interpretation give a credible three-person configuration. Wilkinson, Wright and Hinshaw, among others, also contributed, so there is some arbitrariness, and the shared 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize partly cover the territory.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded by Planck, with all parameters stable; the field is mature. Recognition is, if anything, late, with the unresolved Hubble tension a modest complication but not a challenge to the core results.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and with the 2019 prize may make the committee view the novelty as incremental.
Which team members have the strongest claim, given a large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics into a technology: BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol are original, clean ideas with lasting conceptual and practical influence. The 2022 prize on entangled photons and Bell tests gives a natural link, but QKD itself is a distinct conceptual discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the authors of BB84, and Ekert is the author of E91, so the supplied trio maps neatly onto the two founding protocols. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is an unresolved priority question outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experiments, satellite links and commercial systems have confirmed the principle, but practical security against implementation attacks remains active research. Recognition is timely after the 2022 prize and the field's maturity.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this physics or computer science and cryptography.
Wiesner's earlier priority and the overlap with the 2022 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of the baryon acoustic oscillation peak in galaxy clustering in 2005 gave a standard ruler that independently confirms dark energy and now constrains its evolution. It rests on predictions of early-universe plasma physics and an observed signal, which fits my preference for theory tied to nature.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS luminous red galaxies) and Cole and Percival (2dFGRS) made the near-simultaneous detections in 2005. Theory of the acoustic peak by Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich, and others precedes them and is a complication for a clean allocation.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by several surveys and consistent with the CMB. Recent DESI results hinting at evolving dark energy are interesting but unresolved and make the current interpretation less stable.
uncertainties: Dark-energy implications are in flux with the DESI hints.
Allocation between the SDSS and 2dFGRS teams and the earlier theorists is not clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices provide controllable quantum simulators of many-body physics, from the superfluid-Mott transition to quantum gas microscopes. The conceptual originality of the proposal and the experimental realisations have had wide influence, though the science output so far is more about control than a single decisive discovery.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac made the theoretical proposal (with Jaksch and others) and Bloch led the experimental development; Greiner is also credited for the Mott transition and microscopy, but only three can be named and the allocation is truly contested. The 2012 prize to Haroche and Wineland and the 2001 prize overlap partly.
assessment.maturity: Experimental results are reproduced worldwide, though the promised quantum advantage in simulation of otherwise intractable problems is still being demonstrated. Recognition is plausible but could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: Competing claims of Greiner and others on the experimental side.
Whether a decisive new physical discovery, as opposed to a toolbox, is the right basis for the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new band of gravitational-wave astronomy and possibly informs us about supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic early-universe physics. It is a discovery from nature with an existential reach, and relevant to my own interest in gravity.
assessment.attribution: The evidence was announced in 2023 by NANOGrav (McLaughlin), EPTA (Kramer) and PPTA (Manchester) with a large number of other contributors, so credit is spread across several collaborations and many people. The three supplied names reflect the three major arrays, but it is an arbitrary choice and the individual contributions are hard to isolate.
assessment.maturity: The significance is around three to four sigma with no individual detection, and the origin of the signal remains to be established. Recognition now is likely premature.
uncertainties: Significance does not yet reach discovery level and the astrophysical or cosmological origin is unsettled.
Credit among three collaborations and many individuals is diffuse.
